study.title: Baseline Brain Gray Matter Volume as a Predictor of Acupuncture Outcome in Treating Migraine
study.study_design: Randomized controlled trial with two phases: a baseline period (week 1 to week 4) and a treatment period (week 5 to week 8); two brain imaging sessions
study.randomization: Participants were randomly divided into the acupuncture group and the sham acupuncture groups
study.blinding: not_reported in detail for the acupuncture group analyzed here; single-blinded referenced in prior study citation
study.population: Chinese patients with migraine without aura (MwoA) recruited from outpatient acupuncture departments of Beijing Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine, Capital Medical University, between 2017 and 2019
study.inclusion_criteria: MwoA diagnosed in accordance with the International Classification of Headache Disorders (versions III beta); age 18–65 years; history of migraine for at least 1 year; migraine frequency attacks of more than twice a month; no prophylactic treatments with acupuncture or pharmacological medicine administered in the past 3 months; right-handedness
study.exclusion_criteria: (1) chronic migraine, tension-type headache, cluster headaches, or another primary headache; (2) secondary headache or other neurological diseases, such as headache caused by otorhinolaryngology diseases or intracranial pathological changes, and a history of depression, Parkinson's disease, or other extrapyramidal diseases; (3) relatively severe systemic diseases (cardiovascular disease, acute infectious disease, hematopathy, endocrinopathy, allergy or methysis); (4) pregnancy or lactation; (5) use of prophylactic migraine medication in the last 3 months; (6) MRI contraindications such as cardiac pacemakers or other metallic implants; or (7) alcohol or drug abuse

arms.dropouts: relatively high dropout rate noted in limitations; exact number not reported in main text

extraction_notes.note: The sham acupuncture arm details (sham acupoint locations, needle type, manipulation, and procedure) are described in Supplementary Materials, which were not provided. The sham arm data including clinical outcomes (Table S1, Table S2) and the responder rate comparison are also in supplementary materials.
Expectancy, credibility, and blinding success measures are not reported in the main text. The paper does not mention whether these were assessed.
Deqi and sensory/interoceptive response data are not reported anywhere in the paper.
Adverse events are not reported in the main text of the paper.

The detailed spatial coordinates (MNI x, y, z) for the 10 predictive GM regions are stated to be in Table S3 (Supplementary Materials), which were not provided. Only region labels were available in the main text and Figure 2A.

The hemisphere for 'superior/inferior parietal gyrus' in the correlation analysis is not explicitly stated in the text (r = 0.549, P = 0.0002), but Figure 2A labels it as 'R superior/inferior parietal gyrus'. This is noted as a possible inference.

The exact direction of GM volume differences (i.e., which regions had greater GM in responders vs. non-responders) is not systematically reported in text for all 10 regions. The paper states responders had 'less GM volume in the middle frontal/inferior gyrus and cuneus and greater GM volume in the parietal gyrus compared with non-responders' but does not describe direction for all 10 regions.
The coordinate space is not explicitly labeled as MNI in the main text, but normalization to the 'MNI 152 standard space template' is described, supporting MNI inference.

The total number of patients enrolled and randomized is not reported in the main text. Only the 41 acupuncture group analyzed patients are described. The sham group sample size is referenced in Supplementary Materials (Table S1).
The Rad-score coefficient for the SVM model is described in Supplementary Materials, which were not provided.
Follow-up data beyond week 8 were not collected due to high dropout rate, as stated in limitations.

The neuroimaging modality is structural MRI with voxel-based morphometry (VBM). This is not fMRI or functional connectivity analysis. The modality field was coded as 'other' because VBM (structural GM volume) does not match standard functional modality codes.

The fMRI parameters (TR, TE, flip angle, field of view, matrix, voxel size) reported appear consistent with functional MRI parameters but the study reports VBM analysis. It is possible these parameters were collected as part of a combined fMRI/structural acquisition session, or the parameters relate to a functional scan not analyzed in this paper. The paper describes a structural image preprocessing workflow. Extraction is based on what was stated.

No correlation was found between delta GM volume of left cuneus and delta migraine days in responders, as stated in the results: 'no correlation was found between the ΔGM volume of the left cuneus and the Δmigraine days in responders.' This null finding is noted.
The combination of baseline clinical features and imaging data for prediction analysis is referenced as available in Supplementary Materials; details not available for extraction.
